question: What will U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs report as their total net flow for September 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class is single-day total net flow of US spot ETH ETFs across 2026 trading days; median ~+12 $M with heavy dispersion. Conditioning on the current Aug-Sep 2026 inflow regime (12-day positive streak through Sep 1, BlackRock ETHA/ETHB absorbing ~100% of net creations) shifts the center positive, but the regime is visibly cooling: week ending Sep 4 was +215M vs +816M the week before, and Sep 2 already printed -48M. Ten calendar days out, regime persistence is only moderate. The FOMC decision on Sep 16 (25bp hike priced ~51-58%) sits directly in front of the resolution day, so Sep 17 flows read as a reaction print: a hike likely mutes or reverses creations, a hold likely produces a relief inflow day. That widens the spread and pushes meaningful mass negative (P(neg) ~35%) without moving the median far from the recent regime average. Tails are thin relative to the bounds: 2026's largest inflow day was +226M and its largest outflow day found was ~-129M, so both +300 and -200 require a record-setting print, priced at 2% and 1.5%. Evidence is one-sided in the sense that no liquid market prices this quantity at all - the Polymarket daily sign markets carry <$100 volume - so I stayed close to the regime-adjusted base rate.

Conditioning on the current state moves it up: 13 of the last 14 sessions were positive, ETH is ~$2,458 (+63% off its yearly low) and ETHB (iShares staked, launched March 2026) is a structural new bid. But the streak is visibly decaying - Aug 17-28 averaged ~+158/day, August ~+88/day, Sep 1-4 ~+33/day - and Sept 17 is 7 trading sessions out, long enough for regime-flip risk. I land on a median of +18 with P(positive) ~62%. The main variance driver is that Sept 17 is the reaction session to the Sept 16 FOMC, where markets price ~58% odds of a 25bp HIKE (J.P. Morgan expects the hike, Goldman calls it 'very unlikely'); a hike is largely priced so it is a mild negative surprise, while a hold would be the bigger surprise - this fattens both tails rather than moving the center. Evidence is thin on the exact daily distribution (Farside, SoSoValue and CoinGlass all blocked or returned unrendered tables), so I stay close to the reference-class dispersion rather than tightening. Escape mass: >+300 needs a record day ~33% above 2026's max (+226) - plausible on a dovish-hold melt-up or a large single allocation, priced 3%; <-200 needs an outflow more than 2x 2026's worst single day (-90) on a hawkish-hike shock, priced 2%.

calls.reasoning: Unconditional 2026 daily median sits near +10 (a year of alternating regimes: early-2026 19-day inflow streak, a 17-session/-1.2B May-June outflow stretch, an 8-week outflow streak broken in July, then +1.85B in August). Conditioning on the current inflow regime lifts that, but the regime is decaying monotonically: Aug 17-28 ~+158/day, August ~+88/day, Aug 31-Sep 4 ~+44/day, and Sep 2 already printed -48. Nine sessions separate the last settled data point from the target day - enough for further mean-reversion - so I center at +15, below all three runs, using the Sep 1-4 median (+18.7) rather than its mean (+32.7) since the series is right-skewed. Sept 17 is the reaction session to the Sept 16 FOMC (~55% priced for a 25bp hike): a hike is largely discounted and mildly negative, a hold is the bigger surprise and risk-on - this fattens both tails without moving the center. Right skew is real (2026 max +226 on the late-August rally, driven ~72% by BlackRock ETHA whose single creation basket can dominate a day); left tail is deeper than Runs 2/3 allowed because Run 1's February prints (-129, -113) survive scrutiny. P(negative) ~ 42%.
calls.reconciliation: Four disputes. (1) FACTUAL, deepest 2026 outflow day: Run 1 had -129 (Feb 11) and -113 (Feb 12); Runs 2 and 3 asserted nothing below -91. Unverifiable without web, but Runs 2/3 only ever retrieved daily detail for the May-June streak and never sourced February dailies, while all three independently record February 2026 as among the heaviest outflow months since launch (ETH 3,000 -> sub-1,800). Run 1's claim extends rather than contradicts their evidence, so I adopt -129 as the 2026 left-record and set p10 at -82, deeper than Runs 2/3 and near Run 1. (2) FACTUAL, Datawallet's '+727M March spike': contradicted by multiple wires calling Aug 27's +225.8 the largest single day since Oct 2025; all three runs flagged it unverified. Rejected; it does not extend the right tail. Likewise Run 1's '-165M on August 29 2026' is a Saturday and therefore a garbled date - discarded. (3) FACTUAL, FOMC hike odds 51-58% vs ~58%: same trackers read on different days, reconciled to ~55%, which is variance not direction. (4) JUDGMENT, the center: no evidence breaks this tie, so I take the reading I would bet on - with a right-skewed series the median print (+18.7), not the mean (+32.7), is the correct anchor for a median percentile, and three consecutive steps of regime decay plus nine intervening sessions pull it toward the unconditional +10. Hence +15, outside and below all three runs. Reference class and dispersion basis are carried forward from the runs' shared framing (I agree with them); I widened nothing and tightened nothing, because the underlying sample is news-sourced and extreme-biased. Escape mass: >+300 needs a print 33% above 2026's max - a dovish-hold melt-up or one outsized allocation - at 2.5%; <-200 needs an outflow ~1.55x the reconciled 2026 worst (-129) on a hawkish-hike shock, at 1.5%. Market check on my own: no liquid contract matches this instrument; Polymarket's daily binaries are sign-only, Farside-sourced, and effectively zero-volume, so no anchor and no blend.
